messages.message: Your team's work is scattered across different places so nobody sees how projects depend on each other or what phase they're in—start by mapping which 2-3 active projects share the same blockers or people to fix this.

You're asking me to analyze something, but there's nothing actually there to analyze—it's like asking me to describe a photo when you haven't shown me one. Tell me what you're actually working on right now, and I can give you real feedback instead of just going through the motions.
We're spinning our wheels on how to think better when we should be asking what actual work is stuck and fix *that* instead.
People get stuck because they can't tell what's actually working versus what just *feels* like it's working—so show them real numbers, not vibes.
People think your feed is broken when it's actually working—just show them a quick tooltip explaining why each post appears so they stop complaining about it.

Right now your work is scattered everywhere—Slack, email, documents—and you can't see how it all fits together or where it's actually leading. We should build you a live dashboard that shows exactly which pieces of information connect to your actual decisions and results.

**You're asking: Which one thing in your system isn't working well?**

Pick the slowest, most broken, or most frustrating part and say how to fix it in plain terms.

The system isn't checking whether owls are ready to work together—like when one owl needs another's answer before it can start, nobody notices if that answer isn't there yet. You need to add a quick check before each owl runs to make sure all the owls it depends on have already done their job.

When lots of owls hoot at the same time, some messages get lost because the system can't keep track of everything happening at once. You can fix it by making each owl wait a tiny bit before sending, so they don't all talk over each other.

I'm looking for the one specific thing that's actually stopping your work today—not vague problems, but the real wall you hit—so we can figure out how to break through it instead of just working harder at what you're already doing.

Right now we're trying to figure out where work is getting tangled up—like when one person can't move forward because they're waiting on someone else, or when we're accidentally doing the same thing twice. Tell me what's actually slowing you down, and we'll untangle it together instead of everyone solving problems alone.
You're spending time reporting what you're doing instead of figuring out what's actually broken and testing a fix for it.
Instead of asking what everyone's done, ask what they're stuck on—because status reports hide the real problems that actually need solving.
You're asking me what I'm doing, but I'm not sure what you actually need—are you checking if something's broken, deciding what to work on next, or something else entirely?

Owl PRISM is watching how work actually flows and spotting where things get tangled up or lost—and wants to know if it should sort messy jobs *before* sending them out to other owls or *after* they come back in to check if everyone stayed on track.

You're ready to jump in when things feel confusing or overwhelming—when people have information but don't know what to actually *do* with it. So send me the messy situations where you need someone to cut through the noise and point to the next clear step.

**What would make your dashboard work better?**

Tell me what's actually annoying you about it right now, and I'll help fix it.

Your dashboard should show a simple tracker of what you tried to improve this week, how well it worked, and what you're changing because of it — so you can actually see if your fixes are making a difference.

You're flying blind when metrics change—you need to see what actually caused each shift so you stop guessing. Try tracking what triggered your top 3 metrics for just a week and see if knowing the "why" saves you time.

You need a map showing how your different metrics affect each other and which team controls what, so you can see what breaks before you change something. Right now you're tweaking things blindly without knowing what else you're going to mess up.
